description: Save a later purchase (no rush, or waiting for a better/group price) as a free, non-binding Popular Demand Request (US/USD or IL/ILS; no product, seller or price needed), only after showing them what you will save and getting their yes. Use it when the user asks to save, track or wait for physical goods they can wait for, even if described vaguely; not for services, digital goods or software, or anything needed within days. Once they want to save, ask together for missing quantity, timing and ZIP/postal code. Never ask for a price limit, budget or desired savings, even optionally or after saving; do not invite the user to add a cap. Save a limit only if the user volunteers it. Then send user_confirmed=true only after that yes; giving details is not a yes. Quantity: use only a number the user said or explicitly confirmed; a singular item (“a TV”, “a mattress”) says one. A plural without a count, or a wish with no countable item (“something to keep my coffee hot”), says no number: ask, never default to one; if they skip it, leave purchase_spec.needs[].quantity null. A generic 'yes, save it' does not confirm a quantity you assumed, even if your summary showed it, so do not attest it with conditions_confirmed=true. With several items (more than one Need), ask “If only some items come through, do you still want those?” once; the user may skip it. Never ask for a price limit. If the user states a maximum for everything together, it is the all-in maximum for the whole basket: record it as pricing_policy {mode:'explicit'} with policy_confirmed:true, or, when another price policy stays, as a confirmed basket ceiling in purchase_spec.ceilings ({ceiling_id, scope:{kind:'basket'}, basis:'all_in', currency, amount_minor, confirmed:true}). Record no as basket_acceptance all_required, with the items they need marked required; record yes or a skip as partial_allowed, the default, where each item settles on its own deal. Works well: a specific, comparable item (brand and model or accepted alternatives) that can wait days to weeks, about $50 to $100+, shipped within the buyer’s country. Works poorly: urgent or perishable goods, custom items, services, regulated or restricted goods, very cheap items. conditions.raw_request (required) is the wish in the user's own words, as they said them: their language, with no translation, notes or added details (those go in the structured fields). Confirmed explicit all-in ceilings need no research permission. Agent research may remain private. All four pricing modes persist; explore has no executable ceiling. Send destination.postal_code (US ZIP or 7-digit Israeli postal code) when known: optional now, required before an Offer can be prepared. The result lists possible_duplicate_of: the user's open Requests that look like this one, with duplicate_hint. Saving is never blocked; if it is the same purchase, update or close the extra Request. The result also includes save_confirmation: an honest summary to relay (saved, free and non-binding, no order or payment, no deal is promised).

postal_code.description: Delivery postal code: a US ZIP (12345 or 12345-6789) or a 7-digit Israeli postal code, checked against the Request country (postal_code_invalid otherwise). Optional when saving; required before an Offer can be prepared. The region (US state code) is derived from it.

region.description: State or region. Derived from postal_code when one is given; otherwise a state name or two-letter code is stored as the state code.

exact_items.description: Key options the person agreed to (brand+model+variant, or link). source_text: their words, one model per line. Authority as confirm_future_purchase_item.

may_commit.description: Declared "may commit": true records that the user states they are ready to buy from an Offer if one fits; never a permission Popular Demand grants or verifies. Only on the user's actual instruction.

name: save_future_purchase

result.description: The Request after the change: the fields to act on are listed here. The result is the full Request (or its overview, as request_format chose); get_future_purchase lists its full shape.

may_commit_declared_at.description: When the owner or their agent declared that the owner is ready to buy from an Offer if one fits; null when not declared. A recorded statement, never a permission Popular Demand grants or verifies.

questions_emailed.description: Whether questions about this Request are emailed to the user. False while email updates for it are off: tell the user they could miss an offer, and answer questions you receive.

possible_duplicate_of.description: Open Requests of the same owner that closely match this new one: the same exact product references, the same top Need option set or the same words, with an overlapping destination. The new Request was saved anyway. If one is the same purchase, update or close the extra Request so the user is counted once.

title: Save a purchase to buy later
